KEY MESSAGE 1...A rather convoluted forecast has come to pass as
latest satellite imagery depicts multiple low pressures systems
developing along a stalled boundary stretching from the Gulf to
east of the Bahamas. Each of these low pressures will have an
impact on how the other behaves and what the eventual outcome of
this weekends forecast will be. Trends have begun to emerge as 
well in the forecast with much of the guidance trending towards
the ECMWF solution of a first low moving inland and a second
low deepening off the coast this weekend as they both track 
north. This has at least given clarity to impact timing, though 
exact forecast impacts have a higher amount of uncertainty than 
normal for the timeframe given the fluid nature of the forecast.

The first low is noted in the Gulf and is associated with a mid
level shortwave which is currently tracking E'wards. The second
is noted along the eastern FL coast, and the third is noted 
just north and east of the Bahamas. Latest trends in guidance 
suggest the low in the Gulf and associated shortwave will 
eventually absorb the low over the FL coast and these pieces of 
energy eventually track N'wards along the SE coast and move 
inland across the Carolinas on Sat into Sun. At the same time 
the third low will then track north and begin to deepen as mid 
level shortwave energy transfers offshore. 

Overall this has kept blended guidance rather messy, but given 
the recent trends with much of the Hi-Res, global, and ensemble
guidance winds along the immediate coast have trended lower, 
but the wind forecast has increased slightly well offshore in 
the outer coastal waters. While seas have also trended slightly 
lower, there still remains a threat for dangerous surf
especially Sunday. Combined with high astronomical tides this 
will bring a threat for large surf, beach erosion, and possible 
minor ocean overwash. Confidence is less for coastal flooding 
impacts across the sounds and rivers, especially as the 
forecasted winds across the area have diminished, but given the
developing King Tides, there may be minor inundation for 
locations adjacent to the sounds and rivers.

Rainfall amounts have also trended lower for the area as ENC 
looks to remain between the two areas of ascent with much of ENC
now only forecast to see 0.5-1" of rain this weekend from these
systems. Never the less it will be beneficial rainfall given 
the ongoing drought conditions across ENC.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Overall not much change in the forecast as the 
King Tide Cycle starts second half of this weekend, peaking 
middle of next week. This higher than normal astronomical tide 
cycle is slightly stronger than the one that occurred the last 
week of OCT. The tide levels may be exacerbated by low pressure 
systems that are expected to impact the region, with the first 
this weekend with another potential low pressure system around 
the middle of next week. The strength and track of the lows will
determine where the greatest impacts will occur, but most tidal
locations across ENC should expect elevated water levels with 
at least minor impacts across the typical vulnerable areas. 
Interests along the coast should watch the forecast closely over
the next week for the potential for greater impacts.

KEY MESSAGE 3...In the wake of this weekend's low, a high
briefly builds in early next week. Models continue to show a 
deepening trough moving through the Gulf states and progressing 
offshore of the SE US. This shortwave may encounter a stationary
boundary offshore of SE US and the baroclinic zone along the 
Gulf Stream and produce a sfc short wave or low. The pressure 
gradient would tighten considerably in this scenario, with the 
high sitting over the NE. Confidence remains low at this point, 
but if materialized, we could see a period of strong winds,
elevated seas, coastal flooding impacts coinciding with the 
peak of King Tides, and periods of heavy rainfall. This system
will also have the potential to bring impacts to holiday travel
on Wednesday and Thursday.
